title: Expand ~ in read_yaml()/write_yaml() paths
description:
Expand tilde prefixes with R_ExpandFileName (the routine behind path.expand()) before touching the filesystem, so
read_yaml("~/test.yaml") works.

Fixes #7

title: Wrap long strings when writing YAML
description:
`format_yaml()` and `write_yaml()` gain a `width` argument (default 80; `Inf` disables wrapping). Strings that would produce a line wider than `width` columns are emitted as folded block scalars (`>-`) broken at word boundaries. Folding restores exactly one space at each break, so wrapped strings round-trip through `parse_yaml()` unchanged.

```yaml
description: >-
  some fairly long prose some fairly long prose some fairly long prose some
  fairly long prose
```

## Implementation

saphyr's emitter has no folded-scalar support (`ScalarStyle::Folded` is a `todo!()` upstream), so `src/rust/src/emitter.rs` is a package-local derivation of it (MIT OR Apache-2.0, attributed in the header) extended with:

- **`string_wrap_width`** — wrap eligible strings as `>-` blocks. Round-tripping is the invariant: breaks are only taken at a single space flanked by non-whitespace, and strings with leading/trailing whitespace, embedded newlines, or block-unsafe characters are never folded. Words longer than the available width (e.g. long URLs) stay on one over-long line rather than being split mid-word.
- **Keys are never wrapped** — block scalars cannot be implicit keys. This also fixes a latent bug where a mapping key containing `\n` emitted an invalid literal-block key; such keys are now double-quoted.
- **Root-level scalars are not wrapped** — unindented block content could collide with `---`/`...` document markers.

`width` is validated at the FFI boundary (single number >= 1, or `Inf` -> wrapping disabled).

Note: `R/extendr-wrappers.R` and `src/entrypoint.c` were updated by hand since the wrapper generator was removed in #13 — see the companion issue about clarifying that workflow.

## Testing

- 7 new Rust unit tests (wrapping, indentation, break-point safety, key handling)
- 15 new testthat assertions incl. `width = 40`, `width = Inf`, invalid `width` values, and round-trips through nested structures
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; full suite passes (1332 tests). The pre-existing `canonical_string_tags_cover_all_forms` cargo-test failure is unrelated (fails on `main`).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Port ryaml12 to the savvy native interface
description:
**Summary**
- Port the package from the previous native interface to `savvy` so the Rust bridge is generated and maintained through the new workflow.
- Preserve the public YAML parsing and formatting API while updating the internals that connect R and Rust.
- Refresh the vendored Rust dependency set and generated glue files to match the new entrypoint layout.
- Update the YAML snapshots, docs, and package metadata to reflect the port.

**Notes**
- Internal changes include new Rust handlers, unwind and warning handling, updated `src/init.c` and `src/rust/api.h`, and the `savvy` patch script/workflow.
- Public-facing wrappers and Rd files were adjusted where the generated interface or behavior changed.
- Vendored author and license metadata were refreshed as part of the dependency snapshot update.

title: Refactor Rust/R entrypoint unwinding
description:
## Summary
- Prevent Rust panics from crossing into R by adding unwind-safety handling around the package entry points.
- This change is meant to keep failures contained and produce clearer behavior when Rust code aborts unexpectedly.

## User-facing changes
- Calls that hit a Rust panic now fail through the package boundary instead of risking undefined behavior.
- Added coverage for unwind safety so the expected failure mode is exercised in the public test suite.

## Internal changes
- Added unwind handling in `src/rust/src/unwind.rs` and wired it through the Rust entry points.
- Updated the Rust handler flow and entrypoint generation to route calls through the new safety layer.
- Regenerated the wrapper and entrypoint files to match the updated exported surface.
- Kept the generated artifacts in sync with the Rust-side changes.

title: Simplify AGENTS.md guidance
description:
## Summary
- Reorganize `AGENTS.md` into a shorter, clearer map/notes/validate layout so the repo guidance is easier to scan.
- Preserve the key working rules for generated files, Cargo usage, offline vendor behavior, and Rust style while removing duplicated and outdated instruction text.
- Make the instructions more focused on the current workflow for both public-facing package work and internal Rust build steps.

## Notes
- No functional code changes.
- Internal-only documentation update.

title: Update extendr tooling and vendored Rust dependencies
description:
**Summary**
- Update the Rust toolchain and extendr dependency set to the newer released versions used by the package.
- Refresh vendored Rust metadata so the generated author list now points missing crate authors at their upstream repositories.
- Keep the Rust bridge compatible with the newer extendr API by adjusting list construction and related ownership handling.
- Add a regression test to verify vendored author entries resolve to the extendr repository when crate authors are unavailable.

**Notes**
- Public-facing package metadata now reflects the newer minimum Rust requirement and updated vendored dependency information.
- Internal vendoring files and Rust source changes are limited to the dependency upgrade and API adaptation.

title: Fix Windows ARM Rust target selection
description:
## Summary

- Select the Windows Rust target with an R helper script instead of deriving it from `$(WIN)`, so native ARM Windows builds use `aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm`.
- Preserve existing Windows x86 target behavior, including the LLVM `gnullvm` target for clang-based x64 builds.
- Add regression coverage for the Windows Rust target mapping and the Makevars template.
- Add an experimental `windows-11-arm` CI leg to exercise the ARM Windows build path.

Related to https://github.com/r-lib/Rapp/issues/39.

## Public facing changes

- Source installs on Windows ARM64 should pass Cargo a valid `aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm` target instead of the invalid `-pc-windows-gnu` target.
- No R API changes.

## Internal-only changes

- Added `tools/windows-rust-target.R` for the Windows package build path.
- Updated `src/Makevars.win.in` to call that helper.
- Added testthat coverage for ARM64, x64, and i386 target selection.
- Made the source-file assertions work in both devtools and `R CMD check` test layouts.
- Added a non-blocking GitHub Actions matrix entry for `windows-11-arm` and explicit Rust target installation for Windows jobs.

## Additional notes

Local validation passed, and GitHub Actions is green on PR #10, including `windows-11-arm`.

title: Add package logo
Add benchmarks article
description: Adds a pkgdown article benchmarking yaml12 vs yaml for read/write performance.\n\nAlso updates website dependencies needed to build the article and ignores local benchmark outputs.

title: Improve multiline string emission
description:
## Summary

- Wrap long unindented paragraphs separated by exactly one blank line as folded block scalars, using `>-` without a final newline and `>` with one final newline.
- Keep line-oriented content literal, preserve later indentation, emit empty physical lines without trailing spaces, and retain conservative quoted fallbacks.
- Add deterministic public-API round-trip fuzzing across string shapes, widths, scalar contexts, tags, Unicode whitespace, controls, and mapping keys.
- Use explicit mapping syntax when a key exceeds YAML's 1,024-character simple-key limit or is a tagged collection.

## Public-facing changes

`format_yaml()` and `write_yaml()` now wrap paragraph-shaped multiline strings while preserving the exact decoded value, including paragraph breaks and a single trailing newline. Markdown lists, blockquotes, code, and other strings with semantic single newlines remain literal.

The added round-trip coverage found and fixed three conservative fallback boundaries: newline-only block scalars before siblings, Unicode whitespace at scalar edges, and overlong implicit mapping keys. Public documentation and NEWS describe the updated behavior.

## Internal changes

The emitter carries folded content and chomping policy in one small representation. Literal safety uses the first nonempty line to establish base indentation, block emitters leave empty lines unindented, and mapping-key length accounting includes quoting, escapes, tags, and Unicode characters.

The repository instructions now document that the custom entrypoint layer requires synchronizing `R/extendr-wrappers.R` directly before running `devtools::document()`.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt -- --check`
- `cargo check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo build`
- `cargo test emitter::`
- `Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'` (5,728 passed)
- `git diff --check`

The full `cargo test` run still has the existing `yaml_to_r::tests::canonical_string_tags_cover_all_forms` failure, which reproduces unchanged on `origin/main`.

title: Preserve leading whitespace in literal YAML blocks
description:
## Summary

Multiline strings whose first nonempty line begins with spaces or a tab currently fall back to double quotes. Implicit block indentation cannot distinguish those spaces from YAML structure. The emitter now uses an explicit indentation indicator when needed, so these values remain readable literal blocks and still round-trip exactly.

## User-facing changes

- `format_yaml()` and `write_yaml()` now emit `|2-` or `|2` for literal blocks whose first nonempty line has leading spaces or a tab.
- Existing unindented literal blocks keep their current `|-` or `|` form.
- Mapping keys, all-empty multiline values, and values with multiple trailing newlines retain their existing quoted fallback.

## Internal changes

- Add a focused indentation-indicator check to the Rust emitter while retaining its two-space indentation.
- Cover root, sequence, mapping, nested, tab, initial blank-line, and clip-chomping cases through public R API round trips.
- Update the generated API documentation and NEWS.

title: Add a YAML 1.1 versus 1.2 quick reference
description:
## Summary

Issue #6 asks for a discoverable comparison of YAML 1.1 and 1.2. This brings the rationale from the yaml12 release post into the introductory vignette and links to it from the README.

The new quick reference covers boolean spellings, numeric syntax, timestamps, merge keys, and types that YAML 1.2 removed from its core schema. It also shows the corresponding `yaml12` output.

## User-facing changes

- Adds a YAML 1.1 versus 1.2 quick reference to the introductory article.
- Documents the YAML 1.2 behavior for common ambiguous values and legacy tags.
- Adds a direct link from the package homepage and README.

## Internal changes

There are no code or API changes. `README.md` is regenerated from `README.Rmd`.

Closes #6

title: Reorder write_yaml() arguments and use integer width defaults
description:
## Summary

Reorder the public `write_yaml()` signature so `append` follows `multi` and `width` is the final positional argument. Keep the stream and file behavior arguments together, and use `80L` as the default width for both formatting functions so R does not create the default as a double.

## User-facing changes

- `write_yaml()` now has signature `write_yaml(value, path = NULL, multi = FALSE, append = FALSE, width = 80L)`.
- `format_yaml()` now uses `width = 80L`.
- Named calls keep their existing behavior.

## Internal changes

The wrapper continues to adapt the public argument order to the existing native entry point. Public regressions cover the positional `append` and `width` slots and the integer defaults.

title: Update Saphyr and vendored Rust dependencies
description:
## Summary

Update `saphyr` and `saphyr-parser` from 0.0.6 to 0.0.11 at the current `t-kalinowski/saphyr` `r-patched` tip, `bd5bf962`.

The package keeps a customized copy of Saphyr's emitter, so this also ports the upstream whole-float fix. Values such as `100.0` now retain their decimal suffix instead of being emitted as integers.

## Public changes

- `format_yaml()` and `write_yaml()` preserve whole-valued doubles when their output is parsed again.
- Tagged whole-valued doubles use the corrected decimal representation.

## Internal changes

- Refresh the Cargo lockfile, offline vendor archive, crate attribution, and license metadata.
- Update the transitive Rust dependencies selected by the new Saphyr revision.
- Include the decimal suffix when calculating whether floating-point mapping keys fit YAML's implicit-key limit.

## Notes

- The vendored Saphyr crates continue to support the package's Rust 1.71 minimum.
- This overlaps with the floating-point emission paths in #23. Whichever PR lands second will need to combine the finite `.0` suffix with the non-finite `.nan` and `.inf` spellings.

title: Allow write_yaml() to append YAML documents
description:
## Summary

`write_yaml()` now accepts `append = FALSE`. This allows repeated writes to build one YAML stream when requested while preserving the existing replacement behavior for both single- and multi-document writes.

## Changes

- Public: adds `append = FALSE` after `width`, preserving existing positional calls and write behavior. Explicit `append = TRUE` creates or extends a file.
- Internal: threads the flag through the Savvy bindings and uses Rust append-open semantics for file paths. Standard output behavior is unchanged.
- Adds public regressions for append, create, default, and override behavior, plus positional `width` compatibility.

Closes #4.

title: Preserve non-finite doubles in YAML round trips
description:
## Summary

Fixes #9.

`format_yaml()` and `write_yaml()` now emit R's `Inf`, `-Inf`, and `NaN` using YAML 1.2 numeric spellings, so parsing the output preserves these non-finite doubles. Previously, infinities were emitted as strings and `NaN` was emitted as null.

## Public changes

- `Inf`, `-Inf`, and `NaN` round-trip through `format_yaml()` and `parse_yaml()`.
- `NA_real_` continues to round-trip as a missing double in numeric vectors.

## Internal changes

- Distinguish R's `NA_real_` representation from ordinary NaN values during R-to-YAML conversion.
- Use the same YAML 1.2 special-float spellings for emission and mapping-key length calculations.

## Testing

- `Rscript -e 'devtools::test(stop_on_failure = TRUE)'`
- `cargo fmt -- --check`
- `cargo check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo build`

title: Remove redundant list target protection
description:
## Summary

`yaml12_materialize_list()` previously pushed an existing list target onto R's protection stack before running the batch materializer. The target is passed as a borrow of a live `OwnedListSexp`, which already roots it through Savvy's preserved list. The extra protection required a special tagged-result branch so the error path would not pop the continuation token instead of the target.

This removes the redundant protection pair and tagged-result branch, allowing the materializer to return the unwind-protected result directly. It also documents the rooting contract and Savvy's private tagged-result ABI more precisely.

## User-facing changes

None. The public API and parsed values are unchanged.

## Internal changes

- Rely on the borrowed `OwnedListSexp` to root an existing target for the synchronous C call.
- Remove one `PROTECT`/`UNPROTECT` pair and one result-tag check from mixed-list materialization.
- Document that bit zero is Savvy's private result tag rather than an R flag, and that generated C removes it before resuming the R unwind.
- Add a public GC-torture regression that errors while materializing a string into an existing mixed-list target, then verifies that later parsing still succeeds.

title: Batch R allocations during YAML conversion
description:
## Summary

R allocations during YAML-to-R conversion currently cross a Rust/C unwind boundary for each non-null scalar and each string or name write. Each boundary creates an unwind continuation and enters `R_UnwindProtect()` around a very small allocation.

This PR collects immediate container values in borrowed C-compatible descriptors and materializes them synchronously in C. An all-immediate list can allocate its parent, scalar elements, and names inside one unwind context. A mixed list attaches complex values to a rooted target first, then fills its remaining scalar and name slots in one batch. Handler calls and other complex values keep their local unwind boundaries, so an R long jump never skips Rust frames.

## User-facing changes

There are no API or output changes. Parsing scalar-heavy lists, character data, and nested mixed documents is faster. The added GC-torture regression covers mixed unsimplified containers, nested values, tags, handlers, and simplified character vectors.

## Internal changes

- Replace per-element scalar and string writes with C list and character-vector materializers.
- Batch mapping names and `yaml_keys` values through the same list path.
- Keep complex and handler-produced values rooted while filling the remaining immediate slots.
- Attach fresh elements directly to protected ordinary vectors, following the construction pattern in Writing R Extensions and R's own loops.
- Track borrowed string lifetimes in the Rust FFI descriptors.

The required scalar R objects for `simplify = FALSE` are still allocated. The saved work is the per-element continuation-token allocation, `R_UnwindProtect()` context setup, setjmp, and repeated Rust/C crossing. In the current implementation, `R_MakeUnwindCont()` allocates a continuation backed by a CONS and RAWSXP before each protected leaf.

Inside each C batch, immediate attachment also removes one `PROTECT()`/`UNPROTECT()` pair per character, name, logical, integer, or real element. String-list elements avoid two protects and one `UNPROTECT(2)` call because `Rf_ScalarString()` protects its CHARSXP argument during its own allocation. The parent list and any unattached names vector remain protected across the batch.

## Benchmarks

These are four paired runs against `94b922a`, alternating implementation order with at least 0.5 seconds per case. The table reports the median time across runs; lower times are better.

| Case                         | Baseline |  This PR | Change |
| ---------------------------- | -------: | -------: | -----: |
| Integer list, 4,096          | 769.9 us | 682.1 us | -11.4% |
| String list, 4,096           | 883.2 us | 760.7 us | -13.9% |
| Nested mixed document, 1,024 | 7.554 ms | 6.246 ms | -17.3% |
| Mapping, 4,096               | 1.843 ms | 1.755 ms |  -4.8% |
| Handler-only control, 1,000  | 534.6 us | 535.4 us |  +0.2% |

Integer and string lists benefit from removing a protected leaf per non-null scalar. Nested documents benefit across many small scalar-bearing containers. The mapping case contains null values, which already avoided scalar contexts, so its smaller improvement comes mainly from batching 4,096 names. The handler-only path remains intentionally unbatched and was unchanged within benchmark noise.

title: Build YAML mapping names in a separate vector
description:
## Summary

- Build mapping names in a separately owned character vector and attach it once after all elements are populated.
- Remove the name-specific C/Rust bridge that re-read `R_NamesSymbol` for each representable YAML key.
- Add focused flat-mapping benchmark cases.

## Impact

The public R API and parsed values are unchanged. The conversion path now makes the names vector's ownership explicit and avoids repeated attribute lookup while retaining the existing per-string unwind boundary.

The isolated 4,096-key benchmark was effectively neutral, so this PR does not claim a measurable end-to-end speedup.

title: Allow NULL to disable YAML wrapping
description:
## Summary

Allow `format_yaml()` and `write_yaml()` to accept `width = NULL` as an alias for `width = Inf`. This lets callers pass an optional width through without converting `NULL` before formatting YAML.

## User-facing changes

- `width = NULL` now disables folded wrapping in both functions.
- The width validation message, reference documentation, and release notes now list `NULL`.

## Internal changes

- The shared Rust width parser maps `NULL` to the existing unbounded-width state.
- Public API regressions assert that `NULL` and `Inf` produce identical output.
